arxiv-2101-03084.title: POLAR-2: A large scale gamma-ray polarimeter for GRBs
arxiv-2101-03084.creator: J. Hulsman, N. de Angelis, J. M. Burgess, F. Cadoux, J. Greiner, M. Kole, H. Li, S. Mianowski, A. Pollo, N. Produit, D. Rybka, J. Stauffer, X. Wu, A. Zadrozny, S.N. Zhang, J. Sun, B. Wu
arxiv-2101-03084.description: Abstract The prompt emission of GRBs has been investigated for more than 50 years 50\text{\,}\mathrm{y}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{r}\mathrm{s} but remains poorly understood. Commonly, spectral and temporal profiles of γ \gamma -ray emission are analysed. However, they are insufficient for a complete picture on GRB-related physics. The addition of polarization measurements provides invaluable information towards the understanding of these astrophysical sources.

arxiv-2303-09594.title: One-Bit Quadratic Compressed Sensing: From Sample Abundance to Linear Feasibility The first two authors have contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2303-09594.creator: Arian Eamaz ⋆ , Farhang Yeganegi ⋆ , Deanna Needell † , and Mojtaba Soltanalian ⋆
arxiv-2303-09594.description: Abstract One-bit quantization with time-varying sampling thresholds has recently found significant utilization potential in statistical signal processing applications due to its relatively low power consumption and low implementation cost. In addition to such advantages, an attractive feature of one-bit analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) is their superior sampling rates as compared to their conventional multi-bit counterparts.

arxiv-2307-16653.title: Using Proxy Pattern-Mixture Models to Explain Bias in Estimates of COVID-19 Vaccine Uptake from Two Large Surveys
arxiv-2307-16653.creator: Rebecca R. Andridge
arxiv-2307-16653.description: Abstract Recently, attention was drawn to the failure of two very large internet-based probability surveys to correctly estimate COVID-19 vaccine uptake in the United States in early 2021. Both the Delphi-Facebook CTIS and Census Household Pulse Survey (HPS) overestimated uptake substantially, by 17 and 14 percentage points in May 2021, respectively.

arxiv-2308-14407.title: Identifying topology of leaky photonic lattices with machine learning
arxiv-2308-14407.creator: Ekaterina O. Smolina, Lev A. Smirnov, Daniel Leykam, Franco Nori, Daria A. Smirnova
arxiv-2308-14407.description: Abstract We show how machine learning techniques can be applied for the classification of topological phases in leaky photonic lattices using limited measurement data. We propose an approach based solely on bulk intensity measurements, thus exempt from the need for complicated phase retrieval procedures.

arxiv-2410-06545.title: Signal Watermark on Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-06545.creator: Zhenyu Xu, Victor S. Sheng
arxiv-2410-06545.description: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly sophisticated, they raise significant security concerns, including the creation of fake news and academic misuse. Most detectors for identifying model-generated text are limited by their reliance on variance in perplexity and burstiness, and they require substantial computational resources.

pmc-12993329.description: BackgroundChimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy targeting CD19 has transformed the treatment of hematologic malignancies. pmc-13499866.title: Body mass index (BMI) and forensic autopsy: association with procedural duration, technical complexity and operator vigilance
pmc-13499866.creator: Isabella Aquila, Matteo Antonio Sacco
pmc-13499866.description: Body mass index (BMI) is routinely recorded in forensic autopsy practice and represents a well-established risk factor for numerous natural causes of death. pmc-13550488.title: Pecan nut–derived carbon quantum dots–modified electrode for sensitive electrochemical determination of vonoprazan using a green analytical approach
pmc-13550488.creator: Arwa Gamal Elbanna, Aya Barseem, Hytham M Ahmed
pmc-13550488.description: A novel, environmentally considerate electroanalytical sensor was developed for the determination of vonoprazan fumarate (VON) through modification of a carbon paste electrode with biomass-derived carbon quantum dots (CQDs), representing a sustainable, defect-rich, and effective alternative to conventional CQD-based sensors that rely on synthetic materials and complex fabrication.

pmc-13562892.title: DJ-1-Binding Compound Improves Peripheral Nerve Injury in the Spinal Dorsal Horn by Restraining STAT3-Mediated Neurotoxic Reactive Astrocytes
pmc-13562892.creator: Shengtao Wang, Jieyong Cai, Qingsong Zhou, Ming Zhao, Wei Zhou
pmc-13562892.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Astrocytes are significantly activated after peripheral nerve injury (PNI) and affect the nerve repair by mediating neuroinflammation. DJ-1 is highly expressed in astrocytes, and its binding compounds exert significant neuroprotective effects by regulating antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses. This study is designed to investigate the therapeutic effects of DJ-1-binding compound P-DJ-1A in a rat PNI model induced by spared nerve injury (SNI) surgery.
